chunks: Muhammad is the Messenger of God; and those who are with him are severe with the disbelievers, compassionate among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating, seeking favor from God and His pleasure. Their mark is on their faces from the effect of prostration. That is their likeness in the Torah, and their likeness in the Gospel, like a seed that sends out its stalk, then makes it firm, and it becomes strong and stands straight on its stem, delighting the cultivators, so that it may fill the disbelievers with dismay. God has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds among them forgiveness and a great reward.
ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of the Prophet and his companions as described in Surah Al-Fath?
ai.summary: Known as the Verse of Tawajjuh, this passage is central to Shia exegesis for illustrating the spiritual and physical marks of devotion, particularly the 'seal' of prostration on the faces of the Ahl al-Bayt and companions. It connects the Quranic description to earlier scriptures, affirming the continuity of prophetic leadership, while the agricultural metaphor emphasizes how their steadfastness serves to confound the disbelievers.
